senses.def: to suggest that someone or something would be good or suitable
ex: Can you recommend a good dictionary?
I'd recommend this book to anyone.

senses.def: to advise someone that something should be done
ex: It is recommended that new computers be purchased.
I recommend booking early.

mistake.wrong: Can you recommend me a hotel? / I recommend you to book early.
mistake.right: Can you recommend a hotel (to me)? / I recommend booking early. / I recommend that you book early.
mistake.note: In careful English, do not put the person straight after recommend.

senses.def: an official list of names or things
ex: The teacher took the register.
the electoral register

senses.def: the style of language, grammar and words used in particular situations
ex: Emails to friends use an informal register.
Match the register to your reader.

senses.def: to put information, especially your name, on an official list
ex: You must register for the course by Friday.

senses.def: a detailed study of a subject to discover new information
ex: I'm doing research on renewable energy.
Research shows that sleep improves memory.
She has carried out research into climate change.

mistake.wrong: I made a research about it. / Researches show that...
mistake.right: I did some research on it. / Research shows that... / Studies show that...
mistake.note: research is uncountable, and the verb is do or carry out, never make.

senses.def: able to become strong, healthy or successful again after something bad happens
ex: Children are often remarkably resilient.
The economy has proved resilient despite the crisis.

senses.def: returning to its original shape after being bent or pressed
ex: Rubber is a resilient material.

senses.def: something that it is your job or duty to deal with
ex: It's my responsibility to lock the office.
Parents have a responsibility to protect their children.

senses.def: blame for something that has happened
ex: The manager took responsibility for the error.
No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

mistake.wrong: Who is the responsible of this project?
mistake.right: Who is responsible for this project? / Who is in charge of this project?
mistake.note: responsible is an adjective and takes for. Do not use it as a noun (المسؤول).

senses.def: to finish, use or sell all of something so that there is none left
ex: We've run out of milk.
The car ran out of petrol on the motorway.
I'm running out of patience.

mistake.wrong: The milk has run out of.
mistake.right: We've run out of milk. / The milk has run out.
mistake.note: The person is the subject of run out of. The thing can be the subject of run out (without of).
